features.description: Separate path from query at Muntin's Request boundary and deliver one query value to a handler as Int without manual application parsing.
acceptance: Request boundary in Muntin core: Request(method, target, body) splits the request target at the first '?'; Request.path is the text before it and is the only input to route matching; Request.query is the raw text after it ('' when there is no '?'). muntin.testing.TestClient and the Flare adapter pass the raw target and do not split, parse or interpret the query themselves.

Route matching sees only the path: GET /hello?x=1 -> 200 'hello'; GET /users/42?x=1 -> 200 '42' (the path Int is unchanged, not parsed from '42?x=1'). Every M2-001 behavior without a query is unchanged, including compile-time route checks and first-registered-match-wins.

Public syntax proven to compile on Mojo 1.1.0 and documented in docs/DX.md: app.get["/items?{limit}"](list_items) with def list_items(limit: Int) -> String. The route literal names the query key because Mojo 1.1.0 cannot reflect handler parameter names; binding is positional and docs say so. The number of {..} placeholders in path plus query must equal the handler arity at compile time; a malformed query part (empty, static text, {}, a key containing '=', '&', '?', '#' or braces) fails to compile at the registration call.
GET /items?limit=10 -> 200 '10'; GET /items?limit=010 -> 200 '10' (proves Int conversion happened before the handler); unrelated keys are ignored (GET /items?other=z&limit=10 -> '10').

Query rules, documented and tested: pairs separated by '&'; key and value split at the first '='; a pair without '=' has an empty value; keys compared byte for byte, case-sensitively; no percent-decoding of keys or values; the value is converted with the same strict Int rule as path parameters. A missing key, a duplicated key, an empty value, or an invalid Int (abc, +10, ' 10', 1_0, %31%30, out of range) returns 400 'Bad Request' without invoking the handler. A path or method mismatch returns 404.

Handler storage: the closed Variant is reassessed; the value's source (path segment or query key) is route metadata, so the existing def(Int) arm is reused if possible and any new arm is justified. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md records the arm set and what would add arms next. No unsafe storage is adopted.

Parity: one App registering /hello, /users/{id} and /items?{limit} is driven through TestClient and through real loopback requests to Flare's HttpServer serving the unchanged MuntinHandler; both give the same status and body for /hello?x=1, /users/42?x=1, /items?limit=010 ('10'), /items (400), /items?limit=abc (400) and a non-matching path with a query (404). The adapter contains no query parsing and does not use Flare's query helpers.

acceptance: Production App no longer stores handlers in Variant[def() thin -> String, def(Int) thin -> String]; the M2-003 typed box with pointer erasure, or a strictly smaller equivalent, is the only production handler storage, and App.handle has no per-shape branch.

Unsafe operations live in one internal module with a documented MutUntrackedOrigin invariant, and a canonical check fails if they appear elsewhere in src/muntin or if the module is exported.

features.description: Headers in production, exactly the M3-002 slice: public muntin.Headers, Request.headers and Response.headers, raw handlers reading and writing fields, and the Flare adapter mapping them; no default headers and no typed extraction.
acceptance: muntin.Headers (exported) keeps fields in order with original casing, repeated names as separate fields, ASCII case-insensitive get/get_all, get -> Optional[String] (absent and empty differ), set removing every same-name field, and add/set raising on a non-token name or a value with a control byte or leading/trailing SP/HTAB; it is copied explicitly.

Request gains headers with a defaulted last initializer argument and Response gains headers starting empty; every existing Request(...) and Response(...) call, Response.text and every existing test, fixture and expected diagnostic are unchanged; String results set no headers and no default Content-Type is added, so existing wire bytes do not change.

A raw route receives the request's fields through App.handle's raw argument strings (name, value pairs after method, path, query, body) and its Response's fields reach the backend; typed routes are unchanged; _Call, _Erased, _Route, the storage module, the unsafe surface, App.handle's signature and TestClient are unchanged.

The Flare adapter rebuilds inbound fields from HeaderMap.encode_to verified against len/get_all and Headers.add (any failure answers 400, including a forged name over h2c) and appends outbound fields in order, omitting Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Connection, Upgrade, TE, Trailer and every field a Connection value names, re-checking each through Headers.add and answering 500 on failure; a real loopback request with request and response headers agrees with App.handle except for the documented backend-owned fields.

Production fixtures pin the compiler-enforced invariants of tests/headers_fail; ./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/check_flare.sh and git diff --check exit 0; a fresh-context review finds no unresolved material issue.
